dedupe_keys.name: unalab urban nature labs for nature based solutions in tampere eindhoven and genova

description: UNaLab (Urban Nature Labs) was an EU Horizon 2020 project, grant 730052, that co-created and built nature-based solutions in living lab demonstration areas to strengthen the climate and water resilience of cities, focused on urban ecological water management with greening and inclusive urban design. Its three front-runner cities built pilots: Tampere added storm water retention ponds, biofilters, alluvial meadows and a green wall; Eindhoven replaced paved city-centre areas with green spaces, green facades and a green roof and daylighted a watercourse; and Genova built an urban park with bioswales, infiltration basins and rain gardens. Seven follower cities (Stavanger, Prague, Castellon, Cannes, Basaksehir, Hong Kong and Buenos Aires) and two observers used roadmaps from the project. Coordinated by VTT with 29 partners, it ran from June 2017 to November 2022 at a total cost of about 14.3 million euros, 12.8 million from the EU. The project site, handbooks, a replication framework and a performance and impact monitoring report are accessible online as free HTML and PDF. Caveats: the pages summarise pilots qualitatively, and quantified monitoring results sit in the deliverable PDFs. It illustrates nature-based pluvial flood, heat and water quality adaptation with living labs and monitoring of green-blue infrastructure; related records are the Climate-ADAPT case studies and Oppla.
